54	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
55	
56	/-! ## Separation over the affine opens of a test object -/
57	
58	section Separation
59	
60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
61	
62	/-- The comparison isomorphism of an affine open with the spectrum of its section ring
63	carries `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` to the open immersion of the open. -/
64	private theorem isoSpec_hom_fromSpec {X : Scheme.{u}} {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
65	    hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι := by
66	  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
67	
68	/-- **Separation of test objects over their affine-open test objects**: two morphisms
69	out of a test object `T` agreeing on every affine-open test object `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`
70	are equal.  The affine opens cover `T.left`, and `fromSpecAffine T U` differs from the
71	open immersion of `U` by the comparison isomorphism of `U`. -/
72	private theorem hom_ext_fromSpecAffine {T Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (a b : T ⟶ Y)
73	    (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
74	      Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ a = Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ b) :
75	    a = b := by
76	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
77	  refine Scheme.Cover.hom_ext T.left.directedAffineCover _ _ fun U => ?_
78	  have hU : U.2.fromSpec ≫ a.left = U.2.fromSpec ≫ b.left :=
79	    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (h U)
80	  change U.1.ι ≫ a.left = U.1.ι ≫ b.left
81	  rw [← isoSpec_hom_fromSpec U.2, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hU]
82	
83	end Separation
84	
85	section Curve
86	
87	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
88	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
89	
90	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepGlobalClassify :
91	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
92	
93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
94	  [IsIntegral C.left]
95	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
96	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
97	  [IsDominant pi]
98	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
99	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
100	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
101	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
102	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
103	variable (g : ℕ)
104	variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
105	variable (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
106	variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
107	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
108	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
109	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
110	  ↥(divisorSections k
111	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
112	
113	local notation "DivOver" =>
114	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
115	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
116	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
117	
118	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
119	
120	/-! ## Naturality of the affine classifier -/
121	
122	/-- **The affine backward classifier is natural in the test algebra.**  This is not
123	proved from the characterizing clause: it is forced by the affine package, whose forward
124	map `D.pull` is injective and natural, so its inverse is natural too — concretely, the
125	base change of a classifier classifies the base-changed class, by
126	`D.isDivRepClassify_pull` at the base-changed morphism. -/
127	private theorem overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar
128	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
129	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
130	    (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (F : DivFamZar C A pi g) :
131	    Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F
132	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 B (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F) := by
133	  have hpull : D.pull B
134	      (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F)
135	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F := by
136	    rw [D.pull_naturality phi (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F),
137	      D.pull_classify A F]
138	  refine divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ ?_
139	  rw [← hpull]
140	  exact D.isDivRepClassify_pull B _
141	
142	/-! ## The general-test classifier -/
143	
144	/-- The affine classifiers of the values of `F`, transported to the open subschemes of
145	the affine opens of `T.left` — the family glued by `classifyGlobal`. -/
146	private noncomputable def classifyPiece
147	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
148	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) : U.1.toScheme ⟶ (DivOver).left :=
149	  U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫
150	    (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left
151	
152	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
153	-- The rewrite chain unifies through the section-ring algebra towers over both affine
154	-- opens at once, so it exceeds the default elaboration budget (as in
155	-- `divFamZar.exists_isGlueValue`).
156	/-- The gluing datum: the family `classifyPiece` is compatible with the transition maps
157	of the directed cover of `T.left` by its affine opens.  This is naturality of the affine
158	classifier along the section restriction, applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
159	private theorem homOfLE_classifyPiece
160	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
161	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
162	    {U V : T.left.affineOpens} (hle : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
163	    T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
164	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
165	  have hres : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left ≫ V.2.fromSpec
166	      = U.2.fromSpec :=
167	    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (Over.fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom (T := T) hle)
168	  have hkey : U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫ (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
169	      = T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ V.2.isoSpec.hom := by
170	    rw [← cancel_mono V.2.fromSpec, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hres,
171	      isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, Scheme.homOfLE_ι]
172	  have hcl : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
173	        ≫ (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, V.1) (F.1 V)).left
174	      = (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left := by
175	    rw [← CategoryTheory.Over.comp_left,
176	      overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D, F.compat U V hle]
177	  rw [classifyPiece, classifyPiece, ← Category.assoc, ← hkey, Category.assoc, hcl]
178	
179	/-- The gluing datum: each piece lies over `Spec k` compatibly with the test `T`. -/
180	private theorem classifyPiece_over
181	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
182	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
183	    classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U ≫ (DivOver).hom = U.1.ι ≫ T.hom := by
184	  rw [classifyPiece, Category.assoc, CategoryTheory.Over.w,
185	    ← CategoryTheory.Over.w (Over.fromSpecAffine T U), ← Category.assoc]
186	  exact congrArg (· ≫ T.hom) (isoSpec_hom_fromSpec U.2)
187	
188	private theorem classifyPiece_trans
189	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
190	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
191	    {U V : T.left.directedAffineCover.I₀} (hij : U ⟶ V) :
192	    Scheme.Cover.trans T.left.directedAffineCover hij
193	        ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
194	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
195	  rw [Subsingleton.elim hij (homOfLE (leOfHom hij)),
196	    Scheme.directedAffineCover_trans (leOfHom hij)]
197	  exact homOfLE_classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F (leOfHom hij)
198	
199	/-- **The general-test classifier of the affine package**: the affine classifiers of the
200	values of `F` at the affine opens of `T.left`, glued over the locally directed cover of
201	`T.left` by its affine opens.  The gluing datum is the compatibility with the transition
202	maps `T.left.homOfLE`, which is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar`
203	(`overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar`) applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
204	noncomputable def classifyGlobal
205	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
206	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) : T ⟶ DivOver :=
207	  Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected (X := T) (Y := DivOver)
208	    T.left.directedAffineCover (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
209	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
210	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
211	
212	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
213	/-- The general-test classifier restricts on the open subscheme of an affine open to the
214	transported affine classifier there. -/
215	private theorem ι_classifyGlobal
216	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
217	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
218	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
219	    W.1.ι ≫ (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
220	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F).left
221	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F W :=
222	  Scheme.OpenCover.map_glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected_left
223	    (X := T) (Y := DivOver) T.left.directedAffineCover
224	    (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
225	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
226	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F) W
227	
228	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
229	/-- **The characterizing property of the general-test classifier**: its restriction to
230	the affine-open test object presented by `W` is the affine classifier of the value of `F`
231	at `W`. -/
232	theorem fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal
233	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
234	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
235	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
236	    Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
237	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
238	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, W.1) (F.1 W) := by
239	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
240	  change W.2.fromSpec ≫ _ = _
241	  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Category.assoc,
242	    ι_classifyGlobal hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F W, classifyPiece,
243	    Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
244	
245	/-! ## The two inverse laws -/
246	
247	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
248	/-- **The `pull_classify` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test pullback of the
249	general-test classifier of `F` is `F`.  Both sides are sections of the Zariski vehicle,
250	so it suffices to compare at an affine open, where the characterizing property of the
251	classifier reduces the statement to the affine law `D.pull_classify`. -/
252	theorem pullGlobal_classifyGlobal
253	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
254	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
255	    pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
256	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
257	        (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
258	          (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F)
259	      = F := by
260	  refine divFamZar.ext fun W => ?_
261	  rw [pullGlobal_val, fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, D.pull_classify]
262	
263	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
264	/-- **The `classify_pull` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test classifier of the
265	general-test pullback of `v` is `v`.  Morphisms out of a test are separated by the
266	affine-open test objects, and at each of those the uniqueness theorem
267	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`, applied to `D.isDivRepClassify_pull`,
268	identifies the affine classifier with the restriction of `v`. -/
269	theorem classifyGlobal_pullGlobal
270	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
271	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
272	    classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
273	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
274	        (pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
275	          (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)
276	      = v := by
277	  refine hom_ext_fromSpecAffine _ _ fun W => ?_
278	  rw [fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, pullGlobal_val]
279	  exact (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _
280	    (D.isDivRepClassify_pull _ (Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ v))).symm
281	
282	/-! ## The affine-to-general lift -/
283	
284	/-- **The affine-to-general lift of DDR-9.F7**: an affine divisor package determines the
285	general-test data of `DivRepGlobalData` — the pullback is `pullGlobal`, the classifier is
286	`classifyGlobal`, the two inverse laws are `classifyGlobal_pullGlobal` and
287	`pullGlobal_classifyGlobal`, and naturality in the test object is `pullGlobal_comp`. -/
288	noncomputable def toGlobalData
289	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
290	    DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 where
291	  pull {_T} v := pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
292	    (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
293	  classify {_T} F := classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
294	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
295	  classify_pull {_T} v := classifyGlobal_pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
296	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
297	  pull_classify {_T} F := pullGlobal_classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
298	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
299	  pull_comp {_T _T'} f v := pullGlobal_comp (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
300	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v
301	
302	/-- **Divisor representability from an affine package** (DDR-9.F7): an affine divisor
303	package represents the locally certified divisor functor `divFunctor C π g` by
304	`DivScheme`.  This is the composite of the affine-to-general lift with the categorical
305	packaging `DivRepGlobalData.representableBy`. -/
306	noncomputable def representableBy
307	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
308	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
309	  DivRepGlobalData.representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
310	    (b2 := b2)
311	    (toGlobalData (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
312	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D)
313	
314	end DivRepAffinePullback
315	
316	end Curve
317	
318	end AlgebraicGeometry

section Curve

open Scheme

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- **The chart atlas of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3): each
`Z(♦)`-chart `Spec R_Z` maps to `DivScheme g`, factoring the chart presentation through
`divSchemeι`.  The kill law is `divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` at the chart ring itself
(spelled `Ideal.mk_ker`). -/
noncomputable def divCarveChartToDivScheme
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j))
      ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The defining triangle of the `DivScheme` chart atlas**: through the closed immersion
`divSchemeι`, the chart map of `Spec R_Z` is `Spec` of the quotient presentation
`divCarveChartMk` followed by the pair chart. -/
theorem divCarveChartToDivScheme_divSchemeι
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j).toRingHom)
        ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The atlas factorization of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3,
the DDR-9.F1 keystone): every test morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver` factors,
over a finite spanning family of basic localizations of `S`, through some chart
`divCarveChartToDivScheme i j` along a `k`-algebra map
`ω : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)` out of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring. -/
theorem divScheme_exists_chartFactor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ t : Fin m, ∃ (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
        (ω : DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ω.toRingHom)
            ≫ divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t))))
            ≫ v.left :=
  carveScheme_exists_chartFactor k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) S v

end Curve

8	/-!
9	# F5, the overlap agreement of the forward map (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.4)
10	
11	The affine forward map of DDR-9 is built by factorizing a morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver`
12	through the carve-chart atlas (`divScheme_exists_chartFactor`,
13	`Picard/DivSchemeAtlasFactor.lean:382` — landed), pulling the supplied universal chart family
14	back along each factorizing chart map (`divRepPullAt`), and gluing the resulting locally
15	certified classes (`DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`).
16	
17	Gluing needs the pieces to agree on overlaps.  This file proves that they do, from the chart
18	family's own compatibility hypothesis and nothing else:
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor` — **the overlap agreement**.
21	  Two chart presentations of the SAME `v`, over two carriers `A`, `A'`, restrict to the same
22	  locally certified class over any common `k`/`S`-tower ring `B`.
23	
24	This is the whole of §3.4's family-side W3, and it is free of the DDR9-U ε-identity U2: the
25	overlap of two presentations of one morphism is exactly the input `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible`
26	is stated to supply.  U2 is what will *prove* `IsCompatible` for the universal family; it is not
27	needed to *use* it.
28	
29	What remains for the forward map after this file is the choice bookkeeping (glue, then show the
30	glued class is independent of the factorization) and the two U2-gated laws; see the roadmap row
31	`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep`.
32	-/

93	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower k S A]

106	    rfl

117	presentations `(i, j, ω)` over `A` and `(i', j', ω')` over `A'` present the SAME morphism
118	`v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver`, then the classes they pull back from a compatible universal
119	chart family agree after restriction to any common `k`/`S`-tower ring `B`.

121	This is the hypothesis `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat` consumes, and it is free of
122	the DDR9-U ε-identity: `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` is precisely the statement that two
123	chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled classes, and both
124	presentations induce `Spec.map (algebraMap S B) ≫ v.left` after pushforward.  U2 is what
125	will prove `IsCompatible` for the universal family, not what is needed to use it. -/
126	theorem divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor
127	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
128	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
129	    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
130	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver)
131	    {A A' B : Type u}
132	    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower k S A]
133	    [CommRing A'] [Algebra k A'] [Algebra S A'] [IsScalarTower k S A']
134	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra S B] [IsScalarTower k S B]

136	    [Algebra A' B] [IsScalarTower k A' B] [IsScalarTower S A' B]
137	    {i : (glueData k g r1).J} {j : (glueData k g r2).J}
138	    {i' : (glueData k g r1).J} {j' : (glueData k g r2).J}
139	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] A) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] A')
140	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
141	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S A)) ≫ v.left)
142	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j'
143	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S A')) ≫ v.left) :
144	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A B)
145	        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
146	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A' B)
147	        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega') := by
148	  have h1 := divRepPullAt_comp (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
149	    (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A B)
150	  have h2 := divRepPullAt_comp (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'
151	    (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A' B)
152	  refine h1.trans (Eq.trans ?_ h2.symm)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarGlueKit

/-!
# Zariski gluing of locally certified divisor classes (DD-2 stage S5b keystone)

**The pinned keystone** `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2 — now TRUE at the locally certified level):
compatible locally certified divisor classes over a finite away cover of `R` glue to
a class over `R` restricting to them.

Route: representatives `d i` carry local certificate covers `h i : Fin (m i) → S i`
with certified families `G i l` over `Localization.Away (h i l)`. The composite cover
`r ⟨i, l⟩ := a i l * g i` (numerators `a i l` of the `h i l`,
`IsLocalization.Away.sec`) spans `⊤` (`span_range_num_mul_eq_top`), and the fine
carriers `Localization.Away (h i l)` are `r ⟨i, l⟩`-away localizations of `R`
(`IsLocalization.Away.of_associated` + `IsLocalization.Away.mul`). The fine overlap
carriers `Localization.Away (algebraMap R _ (r q))` receive the coarse overlap
carriers `T i j` by `IsLocalization.Away.lift`; the fine compatibility follows from
the class-level compatibility pulled to the fine overlaps through the two
factorizations of each comparison (witness transport, the composite collapse
`divEq_pullback_pullback`, and the mapAlg-hreg engine for every regularity
side-condition). The certified-input gluing core
(`DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_certified_away_compat`) then produces the glued class, and
the restriction law at the coarse level follows by Zariski separation
(`DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq`) over each `S i` against its fine cover.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
open Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-- Bottom face of a triple tower: `R₀ → A → D` commutes when `R₀ → A → B`,
`R₀ → B → D` and `A → B → D` do. -/
private lemma isScalarTower_bot {R₀ A B D : Type u} [CommRing R₀] [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [Algebra R₀ A] [Algebra R₀ B] [Algebra R₀ D]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A D] [Algebra B D]
    [IsScalarTower R₀ A B] [IsScalarTower R₀ B D] [IsScalarTower A B D] :
    IsScalarTower R₀ A D :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R₀ B D, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R₀ A B,
      ← RingHom.comp_assoc, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq A B D])

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}

/-- **THE PINNED KEYSTONE — Zariski gluing of locally certified divisor classes**
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): for a finite span-⊤ family `g : ι → R` with
away carriers `S i` and overlap carriers `T i j`, locally certified classes
`F i : DivFamZar C (S i) π n` compatible on the overlaps glue: there is
`F₀ : DivFamZar C R π n` with `DivFamZar.mapAlg (S i) n F₀ = F i` for all `i`.
(Uniqueness is `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq`.) -/
theorem DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat
    {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (g : ι → R) (S : ι → Type u)
    [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (S i)]
    [∀ i, IsScalarTower k R (S i)] [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]
    (T : ι → ι → Type u) [∀ i j, CommRing (T i j)] [∀ i j, Algebra k (T i j)]
    [∀ i j, Algebra R (T i j)] [∀ i j, IsScalarTower k R (T i j)]
    [∀ i j, Algebra (S i) (T i j)] [∀ i j, Algebra (S j) (T i j)]
    [∀ i j, IsScalarTower k (S i) (T i j)] [∀ i j, IsScalarTower k (S j) (T i j)]
    [∀ i j, IsScalarTower R (S i) (T i j)] [∀ i j, IsScalarTower R (S j) (T i j)]
    [∀ i j, IsLocalization.Away (g i * g j) (T i j)]
    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    (F : ∀ i, DivFamZar C (S i) π n)
    (hcompat : ∀ i j,
      DivFamZar.mapAlg (T i j) n (F i) = DivFamZar.mapAlg (T i j) n (F j)) :
    ∃ F₀ : DivFamZar C R π n, ∀ i, DivFamZar.mapAlg (S i) n F₀ = F i := by
  classical
  -- representatives and their local certificate covers
  have hrep := fun i => Quotient.exists_rep (F i)
  choose dp hdp using hrep
  choose m h hspan hGs using fun i => (dp i).2
  haveI hImmU : ∀ (i : ι) (l : Fin (m i)),
      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C (S i) (Localization.Away (h i l))) := fun i l =>
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C (S i) (Localization.Away (h i l)) (h i l)
  have hGs' : ∀ (i : ι) (l : Fin (m i)),
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (h i l)) π n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          ((dp i).1.pullback (relCurveMap C (S i) (Localization.Away (h i l)))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C (S i) (Localization.Away (h i l))) (dp i).1)) :=
    fun i l => hGs i l
  choose G hGdiv using hGs'
  -- the numerators and the composite cover
  have hassoc : ∀ (i : ι) (l : Fin (m i)),
      Associated (algebraMap R (S i) ((IsLocalization.Away.sec (g i) (h i l)).1))
        (h i l) :=
    fun i l => IsLocalization.Away.associated_sec_fst (g i) (h i l)
  have hr : Ideal.span (Set.range fun p : Σ i : ι, Fin (m i) =>
      (IsLocalization.Away.sec (g p.1) (h p.1 p.2)).1 * g p.1) = ⊤ :=
    span_range_num_mul_eq_top g S hg h hspan
      (fun i l => (IsLocalization.Away.sec (g i) (h i l)).1) hassoc
  -- the fine carriers are away localizations of `R` at the composite cover
  haveI hAway : ∀ p : Σ i : ι, Fin (m i),
      IsLocalization.Away ((IsLocalization.Away.sec (g p.1) (h p.1 p.2)).1 * g p.1)
        (Localization.Away (h p.1 p.2)) := fun p => by
    haveI : IsLocalization.Away
        (algebraMap R (S p.1) ((IsLocalization.Away.sec (g p.1) (h p.1 p.2)).1))
        (Localization.Away (h p.1 p.2)) :=
      IsLocalization.Away.of_associated (hassoc p.1 p.2).symm
    exact IsLocalization.Away.mul (S p.1) (Localization.Away (h p.1 p.2)) (g p.1)
      ((IsLocalization.Away.sec (g p.1) (h p.1 p.2)).1)

28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
35	  supplies.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
40	
41	## The hypothesis bundle
42	
43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
50	-/
51	
52	set_option autoImplicit false
53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
54	
55	universe u
56	
57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
58	
59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
60	
61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
66	
67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
74	    JacobianData C where
75	  J := J
76	  rep := rep
77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
78	  quasiCompact := hqc
79	
80	@[simp]
81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
85	  rfl
86	
87	@[simp]
88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
92	  rfl
93	
94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
95	@[simp]
96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
101	  rfl
102	
103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
104	
105	section Charts
106	
107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
109	
110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
115	
116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
118	
119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
126	
127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
130	
131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
137	
138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
147	  exact h.symm
148	
149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
150	
151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
158	  have h := hlft i
159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
160	
161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
171	
172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
201	
202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
212	    JacobianData C :=
213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
223	  rfl
224	
225	end Charts
226	
227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# Zariski gluing kit for locally certified classes (DD-2 stage S5b)

The bricks of the S5b gluing keystone (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_pullback`
  — regularity of the two-stage pulled equations from regularity of the composite
  pullback (the Kit's composite germ collapse, member-normalized).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.span_range_num_mul_eq_top` — **the composite-cover span**: for a
  span-⊤ family `g` with away carriers `S i` and span-⊤ families `h i` on each `S i`
  with numerators `a i l` (`algebraMap R (S i) (a i l)` associated to `h i l`), the
  products `a i l * g i` span `⊤` in `R` — by prime avoidance: a prime missing some
  `g i` lifts to `Spec (S i)`, misses some `h i l` there, hence misses the numerator.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isScalarTower_away` / `isScalarTower_left_of_isScalarTower` —
  tower-coherence helpers: maps out of a localization agree once they agree on the
  base (`IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`), and `k`-towers follow from `R`-towers.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_certified_away_compat` — **the
  certified-input gluing core**: compatible CERTIFIED families over an away cover of
  `R` glue to a LOCALLY certified class over `R` restricting to them. The divisor
  assembly is the landed `awayGluedEquations`; local certifiability of the glue is
  witnessed by `mapAlg` of the input families along the identification of each
  carrier with `Localization.Away (r κ)` (`IsLocalization.algEquiv`), divisor-equal
  to the pulled glue by witness transport at the landed chart restriction
  `divEq_pullback_awayGluedEquations`.

The pinned keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat` is
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarGlue`.
-/

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.

/-!
# F4 — the overlap comparisons of the backward Zar classification
(`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §2.1, the step-5/step-6 overlap layer)

The comparison lemmas consumed by `Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`: two `divClassify`
clause-satisfiers for representatives of one Zar class agree on common overlap rings,
and a clause-satisfier agrees with any chart framing of a representative on the
pullback overlap of their tests.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.specMap_eq_of_divClassifyClauses` — the hom-side W3 at the Zar
  layer: clause-satisfiers for `F₁`, `F₂` with `mapAlg B g F₁ = mapAlg B g F₂` have
  equal `divSchemeι`-composites on `Spec B` — `Scheme.Cover.hom_ext` over a frame
  cover of the restricted family, clause transport (`DivClassifyClause.extend`) on
  each piece.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_divClassifyClause_compat` — the `glueMorphisms`
  obligation over the certificate cover: `divScheme_hom_ext` + `pullbackSpecIso`
  conjugation into `S₁ ⊗[S] S₂`, family agreement by `toZar` injectivity
  (`DivFam.mapAlg_eq_mapAlg_of_toZar_restrict`), then the clause comparison.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_chart_divClassifyClause_compat` — the clause obligation
  of the glued morphism against an arbitrary framed test: the framing pushes along
  `includeLeft` (`map_window_frame_toSubmodule` at the identity tower), the families
  agree on `T ⊗[S] A`, and clause transport closes.

All statements are in the `Spec.map (algebraMap ‥)` spelling (I-0237 gotcha (a));
cover-spelled obligations consume them by `exact` (defeq).
-/

/-! ## The total divisor-functor map on locally certified classes -/

variable (n : ℕ)

/-- **The total divisor-functor map on locally certified classes** along an ARBITRARY
test change (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): pull back the representative (the
mapAlg-hreg engine discharges regularity) and transport the local certificates. Well
defined by `divEq_pullback`. -/
noncomputable def DivFamZar.mapAlg : DivFamZar C R π n → DivFamZar C R' π n :=
  Quotient.lift
    (fun dp : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
      DivFamZar.mk (dp.1.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')
          (dp.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R'))
        (dp.2.pullback R' _))
    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
      (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R R') h _ _))

@[simp]
lemma DivFamZar.mapAlg_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
    DivFamZar.mapAlg R' n (DivFamZar.mk d hd)
      = DivFamZar.mk (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')
          (hd.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R'))
        (hd.pullback R' _) :=
  rfl

/-- **The Abel-hook class law at the Zar level**: the divisor-functor map intertwines
the Picard classes with the Čech-Picard pullback, `𝒪(f*D) = f*𝒪(D)`. -/
lemma DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg (F : DivFamZar C R π n) :
    (DivFamZar.mapAlg R' n F).picClass =
      Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R R') F.picClass := by
  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h d => exact Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback (relCurveMap C R R') d.1 _

/-- **`toZar` intertwines the two total maps**: base change of a globally certified
class agrees with base change of its locally certified image — both representatives
are the pulled system (with proof-irrelevant regularity witnesses). -/
lemma DivFam.toZar_mapAlg (F : DivFam C R π n) :
    (DivFam.mapAlg R' n F).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg R' n F.toZar := by
  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h F => exact DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _)

/-- **The identity functor law** at the Zar level: base change along the identity
tower is the identity (`divEq_pullback_id` at `relCurveMap_id`). -/
lemma DivFamZar.mapAlg_id (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : DivFamZar.mapAlg R n F = F := by
  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h d =>
      exact DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
        (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_id relCurveMap_id d.1 _)

variable (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
variable [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']

/-- **The composition functor law** at the Zar level: base change composes over a
tower `R → R' → R''` (`divEq_pullback_pullback` at `relCurveMap_comp`). -/
lemma DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp (F : DivFamZar C R π n) :
    DivFamZar.mapAlg R'' n (DivFamZar.mapAlg R' n F) = DivFamZar.mapAlg R'' n F := by
  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h d =>
      exact DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
        (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_pullback
          (relCurveMap_comp (R' := R') (R'' := R'')) d.1 _ _ _)

end Transport

/-! ## Zariski separation at the Zar level -/

/-- **Zariski separation of the locally certified divisor functor**
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2 — the S5b separation keystone): two locally
certified divisor classes over `R` agreeing under `DivFamZar.mapAlg` on every member
of a finite covering family of localizations agree. Certificates play no role in
equality: the statement reduces verbatim to the S4 `DivEq`-level engine
`divEq_of_divEq_pullback`, with regularity along the chart immersions free (Kit). -/
theorem DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq {n : ℕ} {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (g : ι → R)
    (S : ι → Type u)
    [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (S i)]
    [∀ i, IsScalarTower k R (S i)] [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]
    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤) {F G : DivFamZar C R π n}
    (h : ∀ i, DivFamZar.mapAlg (S i) n F = DivFamZar.mapAlg (S i) n G) :
    F = G := by
  haveI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (S i)) := fun i =>
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (S i) (g i)
  revert h
  refine Quotient.inductionOn₂ F G fun d₁ d₂ h => ?_
  refine DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ?_
  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_of_divEq_pullback
    (fun i => relCurveMap C R (S i))
    (fun y => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R g S hg y)
    (fun i => d₁.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i))
    (fun i => d₂.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i))
    (fun i => ?_)
  exact DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mp (h i)

end AlgebraicGeometry
